# EAFIT students designed a turbojet engine that will be useful in the country's energy transition process

**The plasma turbojet, designed by students from the Turbomachinery research group at EAFIT, will be useful for improving the energy efficiency of various industries in the country.**

**This project was the winner at** _**Innovation Camp**_ **2025, a competition organized by the Ecopetrol Group and the Econova Network, which brought together teams from six Colombian universities around the challenges of the energy transition.**

- [Start](https://www.eafit.edu.co/)
- [News](https://www.eafit.edu.co/noticias)
- EAFIT News: Our Talent Community
- EAFIT students designed a turbojet engine that will be useful in the country's energy transition process

![Image: EAFIT students designed a turbojet engine that will be useful in the country's energy transition process](https://universidadeafit.widen.net/content/9d614eed-98bc-475d-9944-fe94a6556332/web/Turborreactor.jpg?crop=yes&k=c&w=823&h=450&itok=SndipZth)

The EAFIT students presented the Plasma Turboreactor project to judges from companies such as ISA, ISA Intercolombia, Ecopetrol and BATx.

A turbojet is an engine, and the one designed by the students of the EAFIT Turbomachinery Seedbed aligns with the country's sustainability goals, as it is a system that combines some of the most interesting phenomena of quantum physics with engineering principles to achieve a concrete objective: electrifying the air, a process known as "ionization".

This procedure makes it possible to facilitate chemical reactions that, currently, require large amounts of energy and high temperatures, which for economic reasons are usually achieved by burning coal or other hydrocarbons.

As Francisco Javier Botero Herrera, professor at the University's School of Applied Sciences and Engineering and advisor to the research group, explains, “a plasma reactor offers a significant advantage to various industries by drastically improving their energy efficiency. This means we can produce more with the same resources without requiring a large investment. It is, without a doubt, a key and attractive element for achieving the goals of the energy transition.”

Isabella Urán Agudelo, a Mechanical Engineering student, emphasizes that “we at the Turbomachinery Research Group have been working very hard on this project since last year, and more specifically for the last two months. We divided ourselves into four committees: finance, project formulation, social media, and, of course, construction.” This internal organization allowed each member to enhance their skills and contribute decisively to the final result.

And this year-long effort bore its first fruits, as the project won Innovation Camp 2025, a competition organized by Ecopetrol and the Econova Network, which aimed to develop innovative proposals that would contribute to the country's energy transition.

Specifically for Ecopetrol, this turbojet engine will, in its subsequent development stages, halve the energy required for the gray hydrogen production process at Reficar. “And the best part is that it will be 100% electric, which will allow this process—currently responsible for 4% of global carbon emissions—to become independent of combustion, reducing its emissions to negligible levels,” says Santiago Alberto Vélez Casallas, leader of the winning team and coordinator of the research group.

###### Innovation at the service of the energy transition

The creative minds of six teams of engineering students from EAFIT, EIA, UdeA, Pontificia Bolivariana, Universidad Nacional de Colombia, Tecnológica de Pereira, and Universidad de la Costa universities were present at the Innovation Camp. For five days, the participants enjoyed a formative experience that included conferences, workshops, visits, and _pitch_ sessions with experts in the energy sector.

The prototype of a   _plasma turbojet engine_ , presented by the EAFIT students, stood out for its technical approach, its viability, and its relevance to the current challenges of the energy sector. This proposal excelled for two key reasons: “First, it was an innovative and truly disruptive idea, supported by impeccable justification.

This success, in addition to demonstrating the students' academic excellence, reflects the impact of collaborative work between faculty and student research groups, as well as the value of experiential learning. The hands-on experience allowed the students to apply their knowledge, confront real-world challenges in the sector, and strengthen their professional profiles.

![](https://i.ytimg.com/vi/zlU7SY8Dzjw/maxresdefault.jpg)

In recognition of their achievement, the EAFIT team received a prize of 250 million pesos to implement their proposal, representing a concrete opportunity to transform their idea into a high-impact solution.

“This initiative taught us how to formulate a project not only from an academic perspective, but also from a more professional and work-related level, as it allowed us to present the project to large industries such as Ecopetrol, ISA, and other foreign entities,” highlighted Jerónimo Piedrahita Franco, an undergraduate student in Mechanical Engineering.

Para Daniel Tobón Espinosa, profesor de la Escuela de Ciencias Aplicadas e Ingeniería, el solo hecho de participar ya representaba un reto importante. “Ser ganadores nos da mucha más energía para continuar con este tipo de proyectos, sobre todo en el análisis energético y en la solución a las comunidades y a la industria, que finalmente es lo que nosotros como ingenieros siempre buscamos hacer”.
